s: Between which words did the 42nd Amendment insert 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble?
x: They were inserted between 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic', so the Preamble now reads 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.

s: Which of these words in the Preamble was in the original 1949 text and was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
x: The 42nd Amendment added Socialist, Secular and Integrity; Fraternity was in the original 1949 text.

s: What did the Supreme Court do in Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India, decided on 25 November 2024?
o: struck down the insertions made in the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment.
upheld the words ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to their insertion.
directed Parliament to conduct a fresh referendum on the Preamble.
held that the Preamble could never be reviewed by the judiciary.
x: On 25 November 2024, the Supreme Court upheld ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to the 42nd Amendment insertions.

s: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), which clauses of Article 368 inserted by the 42nd Amendment were struck down?
x: Minerva Mills struck down Article 368(4) and (5), which gave Parliament unlimited amending power and barred judicial review.

s: How many times has the Preamble to the Constitution of India been amended?
x: The Preamble has been amended only once, by the 42nd Amendment of 1976, which inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'.

s: In which case were the 42nd Amendment's clauses giving Parliament unlimited amending power and excluding judicial review struck down?
x: Those clauses of the 'Mini-Constitution' were struck down in Minerva Mills (1980); Kesavananda Bharati came before the 1976 amendment.

s: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down 42nd Amendment clauses that gave which of the following absolute precedence over Fundamental Rights?
x: Minerva Mills struck down the clauses giving DPSPs absolute priority over Fundamental Rights, restoring the balance of Parts III and IV and reinforcing the basic structure.

s: Under whose leadership was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 enacted during the Emergency?
x: The 42nd Amendment was enacted during the Emergency of 1975-77 under Indira Gandhi.

s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Abolition of the power of judicial review in its entirety
Freezing of delimitation of parliamentary seats
Addition of new Directive Principles of State Policy
x: The 42nd Amendment curtailed judicial review and attempted to exclude it in certain matters, but it did not abolish the power of judicial review in its entirety.

s: On the recommendations of which committee was the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 based?
x: The 42nd Amendment was based on the Swaran Singh Committee and is called the Mini Constitution.

s: Which word in the Preamble was added by the 42nd Amendment?
x: Integrity was added in 1976; Fraternity, Sovereign and Republic were in the original text.

s: In which year were the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' added to the Preamble?
x: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by the 44th Amendment.
2. The word 'Integrity' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three words, Socialist, Secular and Integrity, were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, not the 44th.

s: Why is the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 called the 'Mini Constitution'?
o: It made sweeping changes to the Constitution
It was the shortest amendment ever passed
It gave the States their own constitutions
It was approved in a national referendum
x: The 42nd Amendment changed so many parts of the Constitution that it is called the Mini Constitution.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Minerva Mills case (1980):
1. It struck down the clauses giving Parliament unlimited amending power.
2. It gave Directive Principles full priority over all Fundamental Rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Minerva Mills struck down the unlimited amending power and also struck down full priority of DPSPs over Fundamental Rights, restoring the balance of Parts III and IV.

s: What does the date 'this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949' mentioned in the Preamble refer to?
o: Election of the first Lok Sabha
First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
x: 26 November 1949 was the date on which the Constitution was adopted. It commenced on 26 January 1950.

s: Constitution Day in India is observed on which date, and since which year has it been observed in this form?
x: Constitution Day is observed on 26 November, and it has been observed since 2015.

s: Which date is mentioned in the Preamble?
x: The Preamble's date is 26 November 1949.

s: According to the Preamble, by whom was the Constitution given to the people of India?
x: The Preamble says 'We, the people of India ... give to ourselves this Constitution', so the people are its source.

s: When was the Preamble of the Constitution enacted?
o: Before the rest of the Constitution
After the rest of the Constitution
Along with the Objectives Resolution in 1946
After the commencement of the Constitution
x: The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution so that it would conform to the constitutional text.

s: Which case held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed?
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable under Article 368, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold about the Preamble in the Berubari Union case?
o: was an integral part of the Constitution and could be amended under Article 368
formed the basic structure and could not be referred to for interpretation
was not a part of the Constitution, but could guide interpretation where an Article was ambiguous
was enforceable by constitutional courts as a source of legislative power
x: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Preamble was held not to be a part of the Constitution, although it was regarded as a key to the minds of the framers and an aid to interpretation in cases of ambiguity.

s: For what is S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) known?
o: Holding that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution
Striking down absolute precedence of DPSPs over Fundamental Rights
Reaffirming secularism as part of the basic structure
Upholding 'Socialist' and 'Secular' in the Preamble in 2024
x: S.R. Bommai (1994) reaffirmed secularism as part of the basic structure; Berubari, Minerva Mills and Balram Singh are the cases behind the other options.

s: In the Berubari case, how did the Supreme Court describe the Preamble?
o: Key to the minds of the makers of the Constitution
x: In the Berubari case, the Supreme Court referred to the Preamble as the ‘key to the minds of the makers’ of the Constitution.

s: In which year was the Golaknath case decided?
x: Golaknath was decided in 1967, after Berubari (1960) and before Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and LIC of India (1995).

s: The Kesavananda Bharati case was decided by a bench of how many judges?
x: A 13-judge bench gave the Basic Structure doctrine in 1973 and held the Preamble a part of the Constitution.

s: Which case of 1995 reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution?
x: LIC of India (1995) reaffirmed the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court call the Preamble a key to the minds of the framers?
x: Berubari called the Preamble a key to the framers' minds; though non-justiciable, it is an aid to interpreting ambiguous provisions.

s: Which case overruled the Berubari Union view that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution?
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution and overruled Berubari (1960).

s: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, the ideals and which other aspect of the Constitution?
x: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, ideals and objectives of the Constitution.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added the words ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’.
The Berubari Union Case of 1960 held that the Preamble was not a part of the Constitution.
The Preamble is justiciable and can be enforced in a court of law.
The Preamble has been amended only once so far.
x: C is incorrect: the Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced in court. The rest are right: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist, Secular and Integrity — the only amendment so far — and Berubari (1960) held it was not part of the Constitution.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Preamble?
o: It is an aid to interpreting ambiguous provisions
It is a source of power to the legislature
x: The Preamble is neither a source of power nor a limit on express powers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble:
1. It can be enforced in a court of law.
2. It is used as an aid to interpretation where a provision is ambiguous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Preamble is non-justiciable but serves as an aid to interpretation of ambiguous provisions.

s: When did secularism become a part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Even before the word 'Secular' was inserted in 1976
Only when the 42nd Amendment inserted 'Secular' in 1976
Only after the Balram Singh judgment, 2024
x: Secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word 'Secular' was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

s: According to Kesavananda Bharati, the Preamble is amendable under Article 368, but subject to which limit?
o: Its basic features cannot be destroyed
Only with ratification by all States
x: Kesavananda Bharati held the Preamble amendable under Article 368, but its basic features cannot be destroyed.

s: Waman Rao (1981) held that basic-structure review applies to amendments made after which date?
x: Waman Rao applied basic-structure review to amendments made after 24 April 1973.

s: Which case held that a State government acting against secularism could be dismissed?
x: S.R. Bommai (1994) held secularism a basic feature, so a State government acting against it could be dismissed.

s: How did the original Preamble of 1949 describe India?
x: The 1949 Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' and referred to the 'unity of the Nation'.

s: Which of the following expressions is found in the Preamble?
x: 'Dignity of the individual' is in the Preamble (fraternity assuring it); 'Federal', 'Fundamental Duties' and 'adult franchise' are not.

s: Which of the following words is NOT found in the Preamble?
x: The Preamble uses Liberty, Equality, Justice and Fraternity; the word 'Freedom' is not used.

s: In the original 1949 Preamble, what did the fraternity clause speak of assuring?
o: Unity and integrity of the Nation
x: The original said 'unity of the Nation'; 'integrity' was added in 1976.

s: In the Preamble, which word comes immediately before 'Republic' in the description of India?
x: The Preamble reads 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic', so Democratic comes just before Republic.

s: Which of the following liberties is NOT mentioned in the Preamble?
x: The Preamble names liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship only; liberty of action is not mentioned.

s:
Arrange the following objectives in the order in which they appear in the Preamble:
1. Justice
2. Liberty
3. Equality
4. Fraternity
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Preamble lists Justice, then Liberty, then Equality and finally Fraternity.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms in the Preamble?
o: 'Socialist' denotes democratic socialism with public and private sectors co-existing.
Indian socialism is a blend of Marxism and Gandhism.
Indian socialism leans towards Gandhian socialism.
'Democratic' in the Preamble is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism.
x: Describing 'Democratic' as a mix of Fabian Socialism and American Populism is not valid; the APPSC G1 2024 key treated it as wrong.

s: A secular State in the Indian constitutional sense is one that:
o: Is hostile to all religious practices
Has an official religion but tolerates others
x: A secular State has no State religion and gives equal respect to all religions; it is not hostile to religion.

s: Before the insertion of the word ‘Secular’ in the Preamble, the word appeared in the Constitution in which context?
o: Article 25(2)(a) relating to regulation of secular activities associated with religious practice
Article 44 relating to a uniform civil code
Article 14 relating to equality before law
x: Before 1976, the word ‘secular’ appeared in Article 25(2)(a), which refers to secular activities associated with religious practice.

s: What does the term 'Democratic' in the Preamble cover?
x: 'Democratic' in the Preamble is not limited to political democracy; it covers social and economic democracy as well.

s: Which of the following pairs of Preamble term and meaning is wrongly matched?
o: Sovereign – Supreme authority, free from external control
Fraternity – Dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the Nation
Republic – Head of the State is elected
Socialist – Head of the State is elected
x: 'Socialist' aims at reducing inequality; an elected head of State is the meaning of 'Republic'.

s: What does secularism mean in the Indian context?
o: A State religion with tolerance of others
x: Secularism in India means equal respect for all religions.

s: What does the term 'Sovereign' in the Preamble mean for India?
x: Sovereign means supreme authority, internally and externally free; the others describe Republic, Secular and Socialist.

s: Towards which form of socialism does the 'Socialist' character of the Indian State lean?
x: Indian socialism is democratic socialism, a blend of Marxism and Gandhism leaning towards Gandhian socialism.

s: Equality of what does the Preamble assure?
x: The Preamble assures equality of status and opportunity, along with liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the objectives in the Preamble?
o: Economic justice means removing economic discrimination and glaring inequality.
Liberty means the complete absence of every restraint on individual activity.
Political justice means equal political rights and access to office.
Equality has civic, political and economic dimensions.
x: Liberty means absence of restraints plus opportunities to develop one's personality, not freedom from every restraint.

s: Which of the following pairs from the Preamble is correctly matched?
o: Liberty – Of status and of opportunity
Equality – Of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
Fraternity – Of status and of opportunity
x: Justice is social, economic and political; liberty is of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality is of status and opportunity.

s: How many kinds of liberty does the Preamble name?
x: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship – five kinds.

s: Which of the following promotes Fraternity in the Indian context?
x: Fraternity, a sense of brotherhood, is promoted by single citizenship.

s: What does Liberty mean in the Preamble?
o: Absence of restraints plus opportunities to develop personality
x: Liberty means absence of restraints on individual activity plus opportunities to develop personality, not freedom from every restraint.

s: Which of the following are the three dimensions of equality in the Preamble's scheme?
x: Equality in the Preamble has three dimensions: civic, political and economic.

s: Of which document is the Preamble of the Constitution a modified version?
x: The Preamble is a modified version of the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru and adopted by the Constituent Assembly.

s: On which date was the Objectives Resolution, on which the Preamble was based, adopted?
x: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted on 22 January 1947; 26 November 1949 is the date of adoption of the Constitution.

s: From the Constitution of which country was the idea of having a Preamble taken?
x: The idea of a Preamble and 'We, the people' come from the US Constitution; its language is credited to Australia.

s: Who moved the Objectives Resolution, the basis of the Preamble?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946; its modified version became the Preamble.

s: On which date was the Objectives Resolution moved in the Constituent Assembly?
x: It was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947.

s: From which of the following is the ideal of Justice – social, economic and political – in the Preamble drawn?
x: Justice (social, economic, political) comes from the Russian Revolution (1917); Liberty, Equality, Fraternity from the French Revolution (1789).

s: The language of the Preamble is credited to the Constitution of which country?
x: The language of the Preamble is credited to Australia; the idea of a Preamble comes from the USA.

s: From which source were the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity in the Preamble taken?
x: Liberty, Equality and Fraternity come from the French Revolution of 1789.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Element of the Preamble)
A. Idea of a Preamble
B. Language of the Preamble
C. Justice - social, economic and political
D. Liberty, Equality and Fraternity
List-II (Source)
1. Australia
2. French Revolution
3. USA
4. Russian Revolution
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The idea of a Preamble is from the USA, its language from Australia, social-economic-political justice from the Russian Revolution and Liberty-Equality-Fraternity from the French Revolution.

s: During which period did the third reading of the Constitution take place in the Constituent Assembly?
x: The formal third reading ran from 17 to 26 November 1949; the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.

s: The idea of Fraternity in the Preamble is possibly drawn from which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
x: Fraternity, a sense of brotherhood promoted by single citizenship, is possibly drawn from Article 1 of the UDHR (1948), not Article 29.

s: Who called the Preamble the 'political horoscope' of the Constitution?
x: K.M. Munshi called it the 'political horoscope'; Palkhivala called it the 'identity card' and Thakurdas Bhargava the 'soul'.

s: Who called the Preamble the 'identity card' of the Constitution?
x: N.A. Palkhivala called it the identity card; K.M. Munshi called it the political horoscope.

s: To what does Ambedkar's phrase 'heart and soul' of the Constitution refer?
x: Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul, not the Preamble.

s: Who described the Preamble as the 'key-note' to the Constitution?
x: Ernest Barker called the Preamble the key-note to the Constitution.

s: Who described the Preamble as the 'soul' of the Constitution?
x: Thakurdas Bhargava called the Preamble the soul of the Constitution; Ambedkar's 'heart and soul' was Article 32.

s: What does the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India deal with?
o: Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States and Union Territories
x: The Eighth Schedule lists the languages, now 22 (Arts. 344 and 351); APPSC asked this in GS 2019 and GS 2025. Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are in the Sixth Schedule, anti-defection is in the Tenth, and the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats is in the Fourth.

s: How many languages did the Eighth Schedule contain originally?
x: The Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages; amendments raised the number to 22.

s: By which Amendment was Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule?
x: Sindhi came by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali by the 71st (1992); Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd (2003).

s: In June 2026, fresh demands were raised for including which of the following languages in the Eighth Schedule?
x: Fresh demands for including Bhojpuri in the Eighth Schedule were raised in June 2026. Konkani, Maithili and Santali are already in the Eighth Schedule.

s: Which Banjara language of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana faces continuing demands for inclusion in the Eighth Schedule?
x: Gor Boli, also called Lambadi, is the Banjara language of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for which Eighth Schedule inclusion is demanded.

s: The 71st Amendment (1992) added which languages to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Maithili came with the 92nd.

s: By which Amendment was Maithili added to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.

s: Who was the chairman of the Official Language Commission set up under Article 344 in 1955?
x: B.G. Kher headed the Official Language Commission (1955); its report was reviewed by a committee under G.B. Pant.

s: In which year was the Official Languages Act enacted?
x: After the B.G. Kher Commission report was reviewed by a committee under G.B. Pant, the Official Languages Act was passed in 1963.

s: Which Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations?
x: Oaths and affirmations are in the Third Schedule; the Seventh Schedule has the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

s: What does the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution deal with?
o: Names and territories of States and UTs
x: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats; the anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule.

s: Which Schedule deals with the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram?
x: The Sixth Schedule covers the tribal areas of these four north-eastern States; the Fifth deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment in 1951.
The 11th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment in 1992.
The 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment in 1992.
The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
x: B is incorrect: the 11th Schedule (Panchayats) was added by the 73rd Amendment; the 12th Schedule (Municipalities) by the 74th, both in 1992. The 9th (1951) and 10th (1985) are stated correctly.

s: The Eleventh Schedule contains how many matters for Panchayats?
x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 matters for Panchayats; the Twelfth lists 18 for Municipalities.

s: Which Amendment added the Twelfth Schedule, listing 18 matters of Municipalities?
x: The 74th Amendment (1992) added the Twelfth Schedule; the 73rd added the Eleventh.

s: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains provisions on the emoluments of the President, Governors, Judges and the CAG?
x: The Second Schedule deals with the emoluments of high constitutional offices such as the President, Governors, Judges and the CAG.

s: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes?
x: The Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes; the Sixth covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Lists in the Seventh Schedule?
o: The Union List originally had 97 subjects
The State List now has 61 subjects
The State List originally had 47 subjects
The Concurrent List now has 52 subjects
x: The State List originally had 66 subjects (now 61); 47 was the original count of the Concurrent List (now 52).

s: Under which provision does the Vice-President take the oath of office?
x: The Vice-President takes an oath under Article 69, not under the Third Schedule, which has oaths for State legislators and High Court judges.

s: Which Article prescribes the oath of the President of India?
x: The President's oath is under Article 60; the Vice-President's is under Article 69 and the Governor's under Article 159.

s: Which provision prescribes the oath of office of a Governor?
x: The Governor's oath is under Article 159, outside the Third Schedule.

s: Which of the following oaths is NOT in the Third Schedule?
x: The President's oath is in Article 60, not the Third Schedule.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ninth Schedule — Land-reform and other Acts protected from Fundamental Rights challenge
x: The Eleventh Schedule concerns Panchayats and contains 29 matters. Municipalities and their 18 matters are dealt with by the Twelfth Schedule.

s: By which Amendment was the Ninth Schedule, the first Schedule added to the Constitution, inserted?
x: The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951; the Constitution had 8 Schedules originally and has 12 now.

s: Which laws does the Ninth Schedule mainly validate and protect?
x: The Ninth Schedule, added by the 1st Amendment (1951), validates listed Acts, mainly land reforms, shielding them from judicial review.

s: With which Article is the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution linked?
x: The Ninth Schedule, which originally had 13 Acts, is connected with Article 31B.

s: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after which date are open to judicial review?
x: The Supreme Court (2007) held laws added after 24 April 1973 open to judicial review.

s: Which was the first Schedule added to the Constitution of India?
x: The Ninth Schedule was the first added, in 1951; the Eleventh and Twelfth were the last, both in 1992.

s: What does Part II of the Constitution deal with?
x: Part II concerns citizenship; Part I covers the Union and its territory.

s: What does Part IX-B of the Constitution deal with?
x: Part IX-B concerns co-operative societies; Part IX covers Panchayats and Part IX-A Municipalities.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Part XII — Articles 264 to 300A — Finance, Property and Contracts
Part XI — Articles 245 to 263 — Union-State relations
x: Part XV (Elections) covers Articles 324 to 329A, not 352 to 360; Articles 352-360 form Part XVIII (Emergency). The other pairs are correct: Part XIVA (323A-323B) Tribunals, Part XII (264-300A) Finance, Property and Contracts, and Part XI (245-263) Union-State relations.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Part XVIII deals with Emergency Provisions and covers Articles 352 to 360.
Part XX deals with Amendment of the Constitution and contains Article 368.
Part XXI deals with Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions and covers Articles 369 to 395.
Part XIX deals with Miscellaneous provisions and covers Articles 361 to 367.
x: C is incorrect: Part XXI (Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions) covers Articles 369 to 392; Articles 393 to 395 form Part XXII. The other Part ranges are right.

s: Which Amendment added Part IX-A, dealing with the Municipalities, to the Constitution?
x: Part IX-A came by the 74th Amendment, 1992; the 73rd added Part IX and the 97th added Part IX-B.

s: Which Articles does Part IV of the Constitution (Directive Principles) cover?
x: Part IV (DPSP) covers Articles 36-51.

s: Which Amendment added Part XIV-A (Tribunals) to the Constitution?
x: Part XIV-A was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, which also added Part IV-A, not by the 44th.

s: By which Amendment was Part VII of the Constitution (Part B States) repealed?
x: Part VII was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956).

s: What does Part XIV-A of the Constitution deal with?
o: Services under the Union and the States
Special provisions relating to certain classes
x: Part XIV-A (Articles 323A-323B) deals with Tribunals; Part XIV covers Services and Part XV Elections.

s: Which Article does Part XX of the Constitution contain?
x: Part XX contains Article 368 (amendment); Part IV-A contains Article 51-A.

s: Which Articles does Part IX-A of the Constitution, dealing with the Municipalities, cover?
x: Part IXA (Municipalities, added by the 74th Amendment, 1992) covers Articles 243P to 243ZG. Part IX (Panchayats) covers 243 to 243O and Part IXB (Co-operative Societies) covers 243ZH to 243ZT.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Parts X and XI of the Constitution?
o: Part X deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas
Part X was in the original Constitution
Part XI was added later by an amendment
x: Both Part X (Articles 244-244A) and Part XI (Relations between the Union and the States, Articles 245-263) were in the original Constitution, so Part XI was not added later.

s: What does Part XVII (Articles 343-351) of the Constitution deal with?
o: Special provisions relating to certain classes
x: Part XVII (Articles 343-351) deals with the Official Language; Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII.

s: As what kind of right does Article 300A recognise the right to property?
x: Article 300A protects the right to property as a legal right, not a Fundamental Right; Articles 31 and 19(1)(f) were deleted.

s: What does Part XII of the Constitution deal with?
o: Services under the Union and States
x: Part XII (Articles 264-300A) covers Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits.

s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with Elections?
x: Part XV (Articles 324-329A) deals with Elections.

s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with the Union Executive?
x: Part V (Articles 52-151) deals with the Union: Executive, Parliament, Judiciary and CAG.

s: Articles 52 to 151 of the Constitution are contained in which Part?
x: Part V covers Articles 52-151 (The Union); Part VI covers the States (Articles 152-237).

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Part)
A. Part VI
B. Part XIII
C. Part XIV
D. Part XVII
List-II (Subject)
1. Services under the Union and the States
2. The States
3. Official Language
4. Trade, Commerce and Intercourse
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Part VI = States, Part XIII = Trade, Commerce and Intercourse, Part XIV = Services, Part XVII = Official Language.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Part VII — Repealed by the 44th Amendment
Article 242 — Repealed provision in Part VIII
x: Part VII was repealed by the 7th Amendment, 1956, not by the 44th Amendment. Article 242 was repealed, Article 2A was omitted by the 36th Amendment and Article 329A by the 44th Amendment.

s: Article 2A relating to Sikkim was inserted by the 35th Amendment. By which Amendment was it omitted?
x: Article 2A was inserted by the 35th and omitted by the 36th Amendment.

s: By which Amendment was Article 329A omitted?
x: Article 329A was omitted by the 44th Amendment.

s: Which Amendment added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection)?
x: The Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

s: The Anti-Defection Law was amended further by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The 91st Amendment (2003) further amended the anti-defection law, deleting the 'split' exception. The law itself came with the 52nd Amendment (1985).

s: What did the 91st Amendment (2003) remove from the Tenth Schedule?
x: The 91st Amendment removed the 'split' exception from the anti-defection law.

s: The special provisions for States under the Article 371 series are located in which Part of the Constitution?
x: The Article 371 special provisions are in Part XXI, 'Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions'. Part XX is amendment.

s: Which Article contains special provisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat?
x: Article 371 covers Maharashtra and Gujarat; 371A is Nagaland, 371B Assam and 371F Sikkim.

s: Article 371J, introduced by the 98th Constitutional Amendment, relates to special provisions for which region?
o: The Telangana region of Andhra Pradesh
The Gorkhaland region of West Bengal
x: Article 371J provides special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka and was introduced by the 98th Amendment Act, 2012.

s: Which of the following groups of regions is associated with the separate development boards under Article 371?
o: Mizo areas, Naga areas, Saurashtra and Kutch
Tribal areas, Hill areas, Saurashtra and Kutch
x: Article 371 allows separate development boards for Vidarbha and Marathwada (Maharashtra) and for Saurashtra and Kutch (Gujarat). Hyderabad-Karnataka comes under Article 371-J.

s: Under Article 371-A, when do Parliament's laws on Naga customary law and land ownership apply to Nagaland?
x: Article 371-A shields Naga customs, customary justice and land ownership from Parliament's laws unless the Nagaland Assembly agrees.

s: For which State does Article 371-A contain special provisions?
x: Article 371-A covers Nagaland; 371-B Assam, 371-C Manipur and 371-D Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: Which Article protects Mizo religious and social practices, customary law, and ownership or transfer of land?
x: Article 371-G protects Mizoram's religious and social practices, customary law and land ownership, as 371-A does for Nagaland.

s: Under Article 371-I, what is the minimum size specified for the Legislative Assembly of Goa?
x: Article 371-I says Goa's Assembly must have at least 30 members, below the usual minimum of 60.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 371-I covers Goa; 371-F covers Sikkim, 371-G Mizoram and 371-H Arunachal Pradesh.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 371-C – Committee of Assembly members from tribal areas (Assam)
Article 371-B – Committee of Assembly members from tribal areas (Assam)
Article 371-F – Special provisions on incorporation and governance (Sikkim)
Article 371-J – Special development board and reservations (Hyderabad-Karnataka)
x: Article 371-C provides Manipur's committee of members elected from the Hill areas; the Assam tribal-area committee is under 371-B.

s: Articles 371D and 371E were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment to implement the Six-Point Formula?
x: Articles 371D and 371E were inserted by the 32nd Amendment Act, 1973, in the context of the Six-Point Formula following the Jai Andhra and Telangana agitations.

s: In which State does Article 371H give the Governor special responsibility for law and order?
x: Article 371H concerns Arunachal Pradesh and the Governor's responsibility for law and order.

s: What does Article 371E of the Constitution provide for?
o: Equitable opportunities in public employment in AP
A Central University in Andhra Pradesh
x: Article 371E provides for a Central University in Andhra Pradesh by law of Parliament; 371D deals with equitable opportunities.

s: Article 371C provides for an Assembly committee of members from the Hill areas of which State?
x: Article 371C concerns Manipur's Hill areas; 371B is the tribal-areas committee of Assam.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 371D — Central University in Andhra Pradesh
Article 371E — Equitable opportunities in public employment and education in Andhra Pradesh regions
x: Article 371H concerns Arunachal Pradesh. Article 371D provides equitable opportunities in public employment and education for regions of Andhra Pradesh, while 371E provides for a Central University there; Article 371F concerns Sikkim, and Goa is under Article 371I.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education for people of different regions of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Amendment (1973), provides regional equity in jobs and education in Andhra Pradesh.

s: How many Parts does the Constitution of India have at present?
x: The Constitution originally had 22 Parts and has 25 now: Parts IVA, IXA, IXB and XIVA were added later and Part VII was repealed.

s: How many Schedules does the Constitution have at present?
x: 8 original Schedules plus 4 added (Ninth to Twelfth) make 12.

s: As what does Article 1 of the Constitution declare 'India, that is Bharat'?
x: Article 1 calls India a Union of States; States have no right to secede.

s: Under which Article is the Finance Commission provided for?
x: The Finance Commission is under Article 280; the Election Commission is under Article 324.

s: What do Articles 330-334 of the Constitution deal with?
o: Reservation of seats for SCs, STs and Anglo-Indians
x: Articles 330-334 deal with reservation of seats for SCs, STs and Anglo-Indians; Official Language is in Articles 343-351.

s: Article 312 concerns which of the following?
x: Article 312 empowers Parliament to create All-India Services. Public Service Commissions are Articles 315–323, the Election Commission Article 324 and Official Language Articles 343–351.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 143 — Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
Article 123 — Ordinance-making power of the President
x: Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission. The Election Commission is provided for under Article 324.

s: What does Article 338B of the Constitution deal with?
x: Article 338B provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes; 338A is for Scheduled Tribes.

s:
Assertion (A): Article 370 provided temporary provisions for Jammu and Kashmir.
Reason (R): Article 370 is now inoperative.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Article 370 gave temporary provisions for Jammu and Kashmir; being inoperative now (since 2019) is its current status, not the reason for its content.

s: Which Article defines a Money Bill?
x: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 123 is the President's ordinance power.

s: Which Article provides for the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
x: Article 143 gives the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction (borrowed from Canada).

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
x: Article 356 is President's Rule; 368 is amendment, 324 the Election Commission and 280 the Finance Commission.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage?
x: Article 326 provides for adult suffrage; Article 324 deals with the Election Commission.

s: Which Article provides for a Commission to investigate the conditions of Backward Classes?
x: Article 340 provides for a Commission for Backward Classes.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Union under Article 1:
1. It is the result of an agreement among the States.
2. No State has the right to secede from it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is a Union not formed by an agreement of States, and no State can secede; it is an indestructible Union of destructible States.

s: Unlike the 'Union of India', what does the 'Territory of India' under Article 1(3) include?
o: States, Union Territories and territories that may be acquired
States and the National Capital Region only
x: The Union of India means the States only; the wider Territory of India adds UTs and territories that may be acquired.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Union:
1. It is not the result of an agreement among the States.
2. No State has a right to secede from it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: India is 'an indestructible Union of destructible States', not formed by agreement, and no State may secede.

s: Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for forming new States amend which Schedules of the Constitution?
x: Under Article 4, such laws amend the First Schedule (States and territories) and the Fourth Schedule (Rajya Sabha seats).

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the admission or establishment of new States into the Union?
x: Article 2 lets Parliament admit or establish new States from outside India; Article 3 deals with forming States from existing ones.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 2 deals with admission of territories that are not part of India.
2. Article 3 deals with alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 2 covers admitting or establishing new States from outside; Article 3 covers changes to existing States.

s: The Union Cabinet's approval to rename Kerala as 'Keralam' began the procedure under which Article?
x: A change in the name of an existing State is dealt with through the procedure under Article 3.

s: On whose recommendation can a Bill under Article 3 to form a new State be introduced in Parliament?
x: An Article 3 Bill needs the recommendation of the President before introduction in Parliament.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Article 3 procedure:
1. The President refers the Bill to the State legislature concerned for its views.
2. Parliament is bound by the views of the State legislature.
3. The Bill is passed by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; Parliament is not bound by the State legislature's views.

s: According to Article 4, what is the status of a law made under Article 2 or Article 3?
o: Not deemed an amendment under Article 368
Required to be ratified by half the States
x: Article 4 says such laws are not amendments for the purposes of Article 368, so a simple majority suffices.

s: Under Article 1, what does the 'Union of India' consist of?
o: States, Union Territories and acquired territories
x: The Union of India consists of the States alone; the wider 'Territory of India' includes States, Union Territories and territories that may be acquired.

s: Puducherry and Goa are examples of territories that India:
x: As a sovereign State India may acquire foreign territory by cession, treaty or conquest; Puducherry and Goa are examples of acquired territories.

s: Under Article 3, to whom does the President refer a Bill on forming new States?
x: The President refers the Bill to the State legislature concerned for its views; it is then passed by simple majority.

s: Through which Constitutional Amendment did Goa attain statehood?
x: Goa is associated with the 56th Amendment; Mizoram with the 53rd, Arunachal Pradesh with the 55th and Nagaland with the 13th.

s: In which year did Nagaland attain statehood?
x: Nagaland became a State in 1963, after Andhra State (1953) and before Haryana (1966) and Sikkim (1975).

s: Arunachal Pradesh became a State through which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Arunachal Pradesh became a State in 1987 by the 55th Amendment; the 53rd was Mizoram and the 56th Goa.

s: By which Amendment was Meghalaya first created as an autonomous State within Assam?
x: The 22nd Amendment (1969) made Meghalaya autonomous within Assam; it became a full State in 1972.

s: By which Amendment were Goa, Daman and Diu added as a Union Territory?
x: The 12th Amendment (1962) entered Goa, Daman and Diu; the 14th added Pondicherry and the 56th made Goa a State.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment made Sikkim the 22nd State of the Indian Union?
x: The 35th Amendment made Sikkim an associate State; the 36th Amendment (1975) made it the 22nd full State.

s: Under which Act was Haryana carved out of Punjab in 1966?
o: Government of Part C States Act, 1951
x: Haryana was formed from Punjab in 1966 under the Punjab Reorganisation Act.

s:
Arrange the following States in the chronological order of their formation:
1. Mizoram
2. Haryana
3. Nagaland
4. Telangana
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Nagaland (1963), Haryana (1966), Mizoram (1987) and Telangana (2014).

s: With which Constitutional Amendment is the statehood of Mizoram in 1987 associated?
x: Mizoram became a State on 20 February 1987 under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 and the 53rd Amendment.

s: By which Constitutional Amendment was Pondicherry made a Union Territory?
x: The 14th Amendment, 1962 brought Pondicherry in as a Union Territory; the 12th did so for Goa, Daman and Diu.

s: Through which Constitutional Amendment did Nagaland become a State?
x: The 13th Amendment (1962) inserted Article 371A; Nagaland became a State on 1 December 1963.

s: In 1960, Bombay State was divided into which two States?
x: In 1960 Bombay State was split into Maharashtra and Gujarat.

s: Under which Act did Mizoram become a State on 20 February 1987?
x: Mizoram became a State under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 and the 53rd Amendment, not the SR Act, 1956.

s: Through which Amendments did Sikkim become an associate State in 1974 and a full-fledged State in 1975, respectively?
x: The 35th Amendment introduced Sikkim as an associate State, while the 36th Amendment made it a full State in 1975.

s:
Arrange in chronological order of formation or attainment of Statehood:
1. Andhra State
2. Andhra Pradesh
3. Mizoram as a State
4. Telangana
x: Andhra State came in 1953, Andhra Pradesh in 1956, Mizoram became a State in 1987 and Telangana was formed in 2014.

s: On which date was Telangana formed?
x: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: Which was the first State in India to be formed on a linguistic basis?
x: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, was the first linguistic State.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the States of India?
o: The figure of 29 States was valid only before August 2019.
Jammu and Kashmir was the first State to be converted into Union Territories.
x: Before August 2019 India had 29 States; the count fell to 28 when Jammu and Kashmir, the first State so downgraded, became two Union Territories.

s: The Union Territories replaced which categories of administrative units under the Seventh Constitutional Amendment, 1956?
o: Part A and Part B States
Princely States and Chief Commissioners' Provinces only
Part C and Part D States
x: The Union Territory system replaced the Part C and Part D States under the Seventh Constitutional Amendment, 1956.

s: As of 2026, how many States and Union Territories does India have?
x: The current count is 28 States and 8 Union Territories.

s: Under Article 239(2), the Governor of which State acts as administrator of Chandigarh?
x: Article 239(2) lets the Governor of an adjoining State be administrator, e.g. the Punjab Governor for Chandigarh.

s: Under which Article does Puducherry have a legislature?
x: Puducherry's legislature rests on Article 239A (14th Amendment); Delhi's is under Article 239AA.

s: Which of the following Union Territories does NOT have a legislature?
x: Lakshadweep has no legislature; Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir have legislatures.

s: Until 1954, under whose rule was Dadra and Nagar Haveli?
x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was under Portuguese rule, not French, until 1954.

s: From which date were Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu merged into a single Union Territory?
x: The merger took effect on 26 January 2020, leaving India with 8 Union Territories.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment gave Delhi a special status as the National Capital Territory?
x: The 69th Amendment (1991) inserted Article 239AA, giving Delhi special status with a legislature.

s: When the Governor of a State is appointed administrator of an adjoining Union Territory, how does the Governor act?
o: On the advice of the State Council of Ministers
Independently of the State Council of Ministers
On the advice of the UT legislature
On the advice of the Chief Justice of the High Court
x: As the President's administrator under Article 239(2), the Governor acts independently of his State Council of Ministers.

s: Under which Article does Delhi have a legislature?
x: Delhi's legislature is under Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991); Puducherry's is under Article 239A.

s: After the merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu (26 January 2020), India has how many Union Territories?
x: India now has 8 Union Territories after the 2020 merger.

s: Under Article 239, through whom does the President administer Union Territories?
o: The Chief Minister of a neighbouring State
The Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Article 239 provides that Union Territories are administered by the President through an Administrator.

s: On what basis did the Dhar Commission (1948) recommend reorganisation of States?
x: The S.K. Dhar Commission (June 1948) preferred administrative convenience, not language.

s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the JVP Committee (1948)?
x: The JVP Committee was Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; K.M. Panikkar was a member of the Fazl Ali Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Fazl Ali Commission was set up in December 1953; Dhar was June 1948, JVP December 1948, and the report came on 30 September 1955.

s: Besides Fazl Ali, who were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Panna Lall and Jagat Narain Lal
x: Fazl Ali chaired the Commission with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru; Panna Lall and Jagat Narain Lal were on the Dhar Commission.

s: Who appointed the S.K. Dhar Commission in 1948?
x: The Dhar Commission was appointed by Rajendra Prasad as President of the Constituent Assembly.

s: Till about which year did the States Reorganisation Commission suggest that Telangana remain a separate State?
x: The Fazl Ali Commission suggested that Telangana stay separate till about 1961.

s: How many States and Union Territories did the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 provide for?
x: The SR Act, 1956 created 14 States and 6 UTs, formed Andhra Pradesh and set up Zonal Councils.

s: On which date was Andhra State, the first linguistic State, formed?
x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's death on 15 December 1952.

s: From which State did the Andhra State Act, 1953 separate the Telugu districts?
x: The Telugu districts were separated from Madras State; the Telangana region of Hyderabad joined only in 1956.

s: On which date did the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 come into force?
x: The Act came into force on 1 November 1956, creating 14 States and 6 UTs.

s: Kurnool served as the capital of which State formed in 1953?
x: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953 from the Telugu districts of Madras State, had Kurnool as its capital.

s: After whose death following a fast was Andhra State formed in 1953?
x: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast for a Telugu State; Andhra State followed on 1 October 1953.

s: Which bodies were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 for co-operation among States?
x: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 set up Zonal Councils besides creating 14 States and 6 UTs.

s: What did the States Reorganisation of 1956 provide for?
x: The 1956 reorganisation created 14 States and 6 Union Territories and also set up Zonal Councils.

s: Who was the chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission appointed in 1953?
x: Fazl Ali chaired the States Reorganisation Commission; K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru were its members.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956; Andhra State came in 1953, bifurcation in 2014 and Amaravati became the sole capital in 2026.

s: For how many years was Hyderabad the common capital under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Hyderabad was the common capital for 10 years, ending on 2 June 2024.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 gives the Governor special responsibility for security of residents of the common capital?
x: Section 8 gives the Governor this special responsibility; Section 95 continues education quotas.

s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 continues existing admission quotas in higher, technical and medical education?
x: Section 95 continues existing admission quotas; Section 8 concerns the Governor's special responsibility.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Its constitutional basis is Articles 3 and 4.
2. Its appointed day was 2 June 2014.
3. Its Tenth Schedule deals with companies and corporations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; companies and corporations are in the Ninth Schedule, while the Tenth Schedule lists institutions.

s: Which bodies were set up under Section 85 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards
Polavaram Project Authority and Apex Council
x: Section 85 created the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards; the KRMB manages Srisailam and other Krishna projects.

s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides a backward-area package for Rayalaseema and north coastal Andhra Pradesh?
x: Section 46(3) provides the backward-area package; Section 46(2) covers Central grants for AP's resource gap.

s: In what population ratio (Andhra Pradesh : Telangana) were cash and bank balances divided under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Balances were split through RBI's books in the population ratio of 58.32 (AP) to 41.68 (Telangana).

s: Which city was made the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2026?
x: In 2026 Amaravati was made the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh by amending Section 5 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

s: Amaravati was made the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2026 by amending which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 5 of the 2014 Act (on the capital) was amended to make Amaravati the sole capital.

s: Which Board set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 manages the Srisailam project?
x: Under Section 85, the Krishna River Management Board manages Srisailam and other Krishna projects.

s: Under which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 are Central grants given to meet Andhra Pradesh's resource gap?
x: Section 46(2) provides Central grants for AP's resource gap; 46(3) gives the backward-area package.

s: On which date was the Presidential order under Article 370, which preceded the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, issued?
x: The Article 370 order was issued on 5 August 2019; the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act took effect later, on 31 October 2019.

s: For which Union Territory has the Ministry of Home Affairs proposed a new Chapter K under Article 371?
x: The proposed Chapter K under Article 371 is for Ladakh, not Jammu and Kashmir.

s: Who was the first Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Ladakh?
x: Radha Krishna Mathur became the first LG of Ladakh on 31 October 2019; Girish Chandra Murmu was the first LG of J&K.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court uphold the abrogation of Article 370 and the 2019 reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir?
x: In Re Article 370, decided in December 2023, upheld the abrogation and the 2019 reorganisation.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First State made a Union Territory — Jammu and Kashmir, 2019
First State made a Union Territory — Goa, 1987
x: Jammu and Kashmir became the first State to be downgraded to Union Territories in 2019. The newest State is Telangana (2014), not Sikkim; the first linguistic State is Andhra State (1953), not Andhra Pradesh (1956); Goa became a State, not a UT, in 1987.

s: On which date did the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh come into existence?
x: The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh came into existence on 31 October 2019 under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.

s: Following the Berubari reference (1960), what did the cession of Berubari to Pakistan require?
o: A resolution of the West Bengal legislature
x: The Supreme Court held that Article 3 does not cover cession of territory, so an Article 368 amendment (the 9th Amendment, 1960) was needed.

s: What was the Supreme Court's position in 1969 on the settlement of a boundary dispute between countries?
o: May be achieved through executive action without a constitutional amendment
Can be carried out only under Article 3
Always requires an amendment under Article 368
Requires a referendum in every border State
x: The 1969 position distinguished boundary settlement from cession of territory and held that executive action could suffice without a constitutional amendment.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement?
o: It was implemented through the 100th Constitutional Amendment, 2015.
51 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 111 Bangladeshi enclaves came to India.
The amendment altered the First Schedule entries of Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.
x: The numbers are reversed: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 came to India.

s: Under agreements of which years was Katchatheevu transferred to Sri Lanka?
x: Katchatheevu went to Sri Lanka under the 1974-76 agreements, without a constitutional amendment.

s: Under the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, how many Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh?
x: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves came to India.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement?
x: The 100th Amendment (2015) gave effect to the LBA; the 9th (1960) dealt with Berubari.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment was enacted to transfer Berubari to Pakistan after the 1960 reference?
x: The Supreme Court said cession needs an Article 368 amendment, so the 9th Amendment, 1960 was passed.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment was enacted following the Berubari Union reference?
x: Berubari held that territory could not be ceded under Article 3 and required an Article 368 amendment, which led to the 9th Amendment, 1960.

s: Which child born in India between 26 January 1950 and 30 June 1987 could NOT acquire citizenship by birth?
o: A child whose one parent was an Indian citizen
A child born to two Indian citizens
A child whose birth was registered in India
x: Children of foreign diplomats and enemy aliens were excluded; otherwise the parents' nationality was immaterial in this period.

s: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, to whom does citizenship by descent apply?
o: Born in India with one parent an Indian citizen
Born outside India with either parent an Indian citizen at the time of birth
Resident in India for five years
Belonging to a territory incorporated into India
x: Citizenship by descent covers a person born outside India when either parent was an Indian citizen at birth, subject to registration of the birth at an Indian consulate.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about citizenship by birth?
o: Citizenship by birth is dealt with in Section 3 of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent suffices if the other is not an illegal migrant.
A person born between 1 July 1987 and 2 December 2004 needed at least one Indian-citizen parent.
For a person born in India on or after 3 December 2004, both parents must be Indian citizens.
x: From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent is enough if the other is not an illegal migrant; both need not be Indian.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Naturalisation – Acquisition of a new territory
x: Birth is based on jus soli; descent is jus sanguinis, naturalisation rests on residence and character criteria and incorporation on acquisition of new territory.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about citizenship by naturalisation under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
o: Ordinary residence of 12 years is required.
The residence period includes the 12 months immediately before applying.
Residence conditions can be waived for distinguished service to science, art, literature or world peace.
No oath of allegiance is required.
x: Naturalisation does require an oath of allegiance.

s: What is the current residence period for citizenship by registration of a person of Indian origin?
x: The current residence requirement for registration is 7 years; spouses of Indian citizens are also a registration category.

s: People of Goa, Pondicherry and Sikkim became Indian citizens by which mode?
x: When a territory joins India, the Centre notifies its people as citizens by incorporation of territory (Section 7).

s: A child born in India on or after 3 December 2004 is a citizen by birth if:
o: The child is born regardless of parents' nationality
At least one parent is an Indian citizen
The birth is registered at an Indian consulate
Both parents are citizens, or one is a citizen and the other not an illegal migrant
x: From 3 December 2004 both parents must be citizens, or one Indian and the other not an illegal migrant.

s: Citizenship by descent is provided under which Section of the Citizenship Act, 1955?
x: Section 4 covers descent; Sections 3, 5 and 6 cover birth, registration and naturalisation.

s: How many modes of acquiring Indian citizenship does the Citizenship Act, 1955 provide?
x: There are five modes: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.

s:
Consider the following statements about acquiring Indian citizenship:
1. Marriage to an Indian citizen is a separate mode of acquiring citizenship.
2. Incorporation of territory is a mode of acquiring citizenship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Marriage is not a separate mode (spouses come under registration), while incorporation of territory is one of the five modes.

s: Under which Section of the Citizenship Act, 1955 is citizenship acquired by naturalisation?
x: Section 6 deals with naturalisation; Section 5 is registration and Section 7 is incorporation of territory.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Mode of acquisition)
A. Birth
B. Registration
C. Naturalisation
D. Incorporation of territory
List-II (Section of Citizenship Act, 1955)
1. Section 7
2. Section 3
3. Section 6
4. Section 5
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Birth = Section 3, Registration = Section 5, Naturalisation = Section 6, Incorporation of territory = Section 7.

s:
Assertion (A): Section 3 of the Citizenship Act, 1955 deals with citizenship by birth.
Reason (R): Section 7 of the Act deals with citizenship by registration.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Section 3 covers citizenship by birth, so A is true; Section 7 covers incorporation of territory (registration is Section 5), so R is false.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Part II of the Constitution?
o: It deals only with persons who were citizens at the commencement of the Constitution.
Article 10 provides for continuance of citizenship, subject to laws made by Parliament.
Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law.
Article 10 empowers Parliament to regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship.
x: Parliament's power to regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship is in Article 11, not Article 10.

s: Under Article 5, which of the following is one of the conditions connected with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution?
o: Residence in India for at least 5 years prior to 1950
Registration with the Election Commission before 1950
Residence in India for at least 2 years prior to 1950
Ownership of property in India before 1950
x: Article 5 conferred citizenship on persons domiciled in India who were born in India, had a parent born in India, or had lived in India for at least five years before 1950. Two years and property ownership are distractors.

s: What was the permit cut-off date under Article 6 for persons who migrated from Pakistan?
x: Article 6 turns on migration before or after 19 July 1948; 1 March 1947 is the date relevant to Article 7.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the rights of certain persons who migrated to Pakistan?
x: Article 7 covers migrants to Pakistan; Article 6 covers persons who migrated from Pakistan to India.

s: To whom are the freedoms under Article 19 available?
x: Article 19 freedoms, like Articles 15, 16, 29 and 30, are available only to citizens.

s: Which Article provides for the continuance of the rights of citizenship, subject to Parliament's law?
x: Article 10 provides for continuance of citizenship rights; Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship.

s: Under which Article could persons of Indian origin residing abroad become citizens by registering at an Indian diplomatic or consular office?
x: Article 8 covers persons of Indian origin abroad; Article 9 deals with voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.

s: What does Article 9 of the Constitution deal with?
o: Continuance of the rights of citizenship
Loss of citizenship on voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship
x: Article 9 provides automatic loss of Indian citizenship when a person voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship.

s: Unlike in the USA, to whom is the office of President in India open?
o: Both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens
x: In India both citizens by birth and naturalised citizens can become President; in the USA only a natural-born citizen can.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Only a citizen of India can hold the office of Attorney General of India.
2. Only a citizen of India can be appointed Governor of a State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Offices such as President, Vice-President, judges, Governor and Attorney General are open only to citizens.

s: Which of the following countries follow the principle of dual citizenship at the national and sub-national levels?
o: The United States of America and Switzerland
x: The United States and Switzerland recognise national as well as state or cantonal citizenship. India follows single citizenship.

s: From which country's constitutional practice was India's system of single citizenship chiefly borrowed?
x: The Indian Constitution adopted the idea of single citizenship from Britain. Canada also follows single citizenship.

s:
Consider the following statements about citizenship in India:
1. There is a single domicile for the Union and the States.
2. States may grant a separate State citizenship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India has single citizenship and a single domicile; there is no separate State citizenship.

s: How is the broad basis of Indian citizenship said to have shifted?
o: From jus sanguinis to jus soli
From jus soli to jus sanguinis
x: India has moved from jus soli (citizenship by place of birth) towards jus sanguinis (citizenship by descent).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The PIO card was merged with the OCI card in 2015. The 2003 amendment related to the birth rule and OCI registration, while the CAA route belongs to 2019.

s: Which Citizenship (Amendment) Act introduced OCI registration and Section 14A?
x: The 2003 amendment introduced OCI and Sec. 14A; the 2005 amendment widened OCI and the 2015 amendment merged PIO and OCI.

s: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act, 1955 NOT amended?
x: The stated chronology identifies 1986, 2003 and 2019 amendments, while 2008 is specified as a year in which the Act was not amended.

s: Which Citizenship (Amendment) Act required at least one parent to be an Indian citizen for birth in India from 1 July 1987?
x: The 1986 Act made this change effective from 1 July 1987; there is no separate 1987 amendment.

s: What did the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005 do?
o: Merged the PIO card with OCI
Cut the naturalisation period to 5 years
x: The 2005 Act widened OCI; the PIO merger came in 2015 and Section 14A in 2003.

s: How many religious communities are specified under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
x: The six specified communities are Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian; Muslims are not included.

s: To how many years did the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduce the residence requirement for naturalisation?
x: The CAA 2019 reduced the naturalisation residence requirement to five years and gives citizenship effect from the date of entry.

s: On which date did the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules under the CAA, 2019 become effective?
x: The CAA was enacted on 12 December 2019, while its Rules became effective on 11 March 2024.

s: Under the MHA order of 19 August 2026, who processes CAA applications in the specified eight States and UTs?
x: The 19 August 2026 order transferred processing in the eight States and UTs to District Collectors instead of Empowered Committees.

s: With reference to which Article has the constitutional validity of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 mainly been challenged?
x: The challenge principally invokes Article 14, particularly concerning classification based on religion and country.

s: What must a CAA applicant holding a passport of Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh do under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: Retain the passport permanently after approval
Exchange the passport for an OCI card within seven years
File an affidavit concerning the passport and surrender it within 15 days of approval
Surrender the passport before entering India and file no affidavit
x: The applicant must file an affidavit concerning the relevant passport and surrender the passport within 15 days after approval.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 is incorrect?
o: The relevant entry cut-off date is 31 December 2014.
It concerns six non-Muslim persecuted minorities.
It applies to persons who entered India after 31 December 2014.
It concerns persons from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
x: C is incorrect: the CAA covers those who entered India on or before 31 December 2014, not after. The other statements are right.

s: Along with Inner Line Permit areas, which areas are exempted from the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
o: Sixth Schedule tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura
x: The Sixth Schedule tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura and the Inner Line Permit areas are exempt; West Bengal's districts are not.

s: The CAA, 2019 covers specified migrants who entered India on or before which date?
x: The cut-off is entry on or before 31 December 2014; citizenship counts from the date of entry.

s: On which date did the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2019 receive the President's assent?
x: Assent came on 12 December 2019; Lok Sabha passed it on 9 December, Rajya Sabha on 11 December, and the Rules took effect on 11 March 2024.

s: Which of the following countries is NOT covered by the CAA, 2019?
x: The CAA covers only Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.

s: From which date is citizenship granted under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 counted?
o: The date of entry into India
x: Under the CAA, 2019 citizenship counts from the date of entry into India.

s: The challenge to the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 is being heard by a Supreme Court Bench headed by which Chief Justice of India?
x: More than 250 petitions against the CAA are before a Bench under CJI Surya Kant; final hearing began on 5 May 2026.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted by Parliament.
The Election Commission has exclusive constitutional power to regulate citizenship.
Article 11 deals with Parliament's power to regulate citizenship by law.
Citizenship Rules are made under Section 18.
x: B is incorrect: the Election Commission has no power over citizenship; Parliament alone regulates it under Article 11 (Citizenship Act, 1955, with Rules under Section 18).

s: Under which Article does the Election Commission check citizenship in relation to electoral rolls?
x: The Election Commission checks citizenship for electoral rolls under Article 324, while the Union Home Ministry frames citizenship rules.

s: Who is a Person of Indian Origin (PIO), as distinct from an NRI?
o: A foreign citizen of Indian origin
An Indian citizen of foreign origin
A stateless person of Indian origin
x: A PIO is a foreign citizen whose ancestors were Indian nationals, whereas an NRI is an Indian citizen ordinarily residing abroad.

s: Which of the following does an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder enjoy?
o: The right to vote in Indian elections
Eligibility to contest Lok Sabha elections
x: OCI cardholders are foreign nationals of Indian origin with a lifelong visa facility; they cannot vote as OCI cardholders.

s: A person is barred from an OCI card if the person or a parent or grandparent was a citizen of which countries?
x: Those who are or were, or whose parents or grandparents were, citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are barred from OCI.

s: Which of the following was introduced for OCI services by the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: Merger of PIO and OCI cards
x: The 2026 Rules introduced e-OCI cards, a central OCI database and online application and renunciation; the PIO-OCI merger was in 2015.

s: Who is a Non-Resident Indian (NRI)?
o: An Indian citizen ordinarily residing abroad
A foreign citizen whose ancestors were Indian nationals
A foreign national registered under Section 7A
A citizen of any Commonwealth country
x: An NRI is an Indian citizen living abroad with an Indian passport; PIO and OCI holders are foreign citizens.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NRI – Foreign citizen of Indian origin
PIO card – Merged with OCI in 2005
Commonwealth citizen – Indian citizen living abroad
x: OCI holders are registered under Section 7A; an NRI is an Indian citizen and the PIO card merged with OCI in 2015.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about OCI cardholders?
o: They are not citizens of India.
They can vote in Lok Sabha elections.
x: OCI cardholders cannot vote or contest elections, as they are not citizens.

s: What does Section 14A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 provide for?
o: The merger of PIO and OCI cards
The National Register of Indian Citizens and a national identity card
x: Section 14A provides for the National Register of Indian Citizens and the issue of a national identity card.

s: Deprivation of Indian citizenship by the Central Government applies only to citizens by which mode?
x: The Centre may deprive only citizens by naturalisation, registration or Art. 5(c), on grounds such as fraud, disloyalty or aiding an enemy.

s: Minor children of a person who renounces Indian citizenship may resume citizenship within how long after attaining majority?
x: Renunciation is by declaration; minor children also lose citizenship but may resume it within one year of attaining majority.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Section 9 deals with termination of citizenship, whereas Section 10 deals with deprivation of citizenship. Section 8 concerns renunciation and Section 7A concerns OCI cardholders.

s: What is compulsory termination of Indian citizenship by the Central Government called?
x: Deprivation is compulsory termination by the Centre; renunciation is a voluntary surrender by the citizen.

s: For at least how long must a naturalised or registered citizen be imprisoned within five years of naturalisation or registration to be deprived of citizenship?
x: Under Section 10, two years' imprisonment within five years of naturalisation or registration is a ground, along with fraud, disloyalty and unlawful trade with an enemy.

s: Which Section of the Citizenship Act, 1955 permits the Central Government to compulsorily deprive a naturalised citizen of citizenship?
x: Section 10 lets the Central Government deprive a naturalised or registered citizen of citizenship on grounds such as fraud or disloyalty.

s: What is the effect, by itself, of an Indian citizen marrying a foreign citizen?
o: It has no effect on citizenship
The Centre must deprive the person of citizenship
Citizenship must be renounced within one year
x: Marrying a foreigner, like criticising the government, does not by itself take away Indian citizenship.

s: Under Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, when does termination of citizenship occur?
o: Voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country
x: Termination is automatic on voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship; renunciation is Section 8 and fraud leads to deprivation.

s: What does Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 deal with?
x: Section 7A covers registration of OCI cardholders; Section 14A is the NRIC and Section 18 the rule-making power.

s: How many modes of losing Indian citizenship are laid down in the Citizenship Act, 1955?
x: Citizenship is lost in three ways: renunciation, termination and deprivation.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NPR — persons granted citizenship under the CAA alone
x: The National Register of Citizens concerns citizens only, whereas the National Population Register covers all usual residents. Thus, NRC—citizens only is correctly matched.

s: Of which of the following is the National Register of Citizens (NRC) a subset?
x: The NRC covers citizens only and is a subset of the NPR, which lists all usual residents.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Register of Citizens (NRC) covers all usual residents of India.
2. A draft NRC has been published for Assam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NRC lists citizens only (the NPR covers all usual residents); a draft NRC was published for Assam.

s: Under Section 9 of which Act is it stated that the number issued under it is not a proof of citizenship?
x: Section 9 of the Aadhaar Act says Aadhaar is proof of identity only, not of citizenship.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the present number and original number of groups of Fundamental Rights?
x: The Constitution originally contained seven groups of Fundamental Rights. The right to property was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment, leaving six groups at present.

s: After the 44th Amendment, 1978, under which Article is the right to property protected?
x: The 44th Amendment removed property from Part III; it is now a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

s: Where are the Fundamental Rights, often described as the 'Magna Carta of India', contained?
x: Fundamental Rights are in Part III, Articles 12 to 35 (Art. 12 defines State, Art. 13 voids inconsistent laws, Arts. 33-35 cover limits and legislation). Part IV (Arts. 36-51) holds the Directive Principles and Part IVA (Art. 51A) the Fundamental Duties; Arts. 14-32 is only the span of the six groups, not the whole Part.

s: Which Articles contain the right to freedom of religion?
x: Freedom of religion is in Articles 25-28; equality is 14-18, exploitation 23-24 and cultural and educational rights 29-30.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Right to Freedom of Religion – Article 32
x: The Right against Exploitation is Articles 23–24; Equality is 14–18, Freedom of Religion 25–28 and Constitutional Remedies Article 32.

s: Which Articles make up the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
x: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is Article 32 alone, not Articles 30-32.

s: Who described Fundamental Rights as 'a pledge to our people and a pact with the civilised world'?
x: The description is attributed to S. Radhakrishnan.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Part III of the Constitution contains Articles 12 to 35.
The Right against Exploitation covers Articles 23 to 24.
The Right to Constitutional Remedies covers Articles 30 to 32.
The Right to Equality covers Articles 14 to 18.
x: C is incorrect: the Right to Constitutional Remedies is Article 32 alone; Articles 29–30 are cultural and educational rights. Part III (12–35), exploitation (23–24) and equality (14–18) are stated correctly.

s: Under which group of Fundamental Rights does Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) fall?
